definitions_note: AUDIT STRATUM - never pooled with generation experiments; all generation outcome cells left blank by design. Corpus as printed: four corpora, Jan 2020-Aug 2025 - arXiv 1,465,145 preprints with 44,107,529 citations; bioRxiv 261,928 preprints with 21,183,111 citations; SSRN 421,698 preprints with 26,815,043 citations (via Crossref); PubMed Central 10% random sample, 374,807 manuscripts (2020-2025) with 19,245,787 references. Headline totals as printed in the abstract: '111 million references across 2.5 million papers in arXiv, bioRxiv, SSRN, and PubMed Central' (per-corpus figures sum to 2,523,578 papers and 111,351,470 references). Denominator: published references (and papers) in the corpora, NOT generated references. Detection method as printed: references with non-existent titles; titles matched against a locally hosted Elasticsearch index from Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex (95.1% matched), unmatched entries cleaned with GPT-4o-mini (unmatched rate 2.33%, then 1.54% after title re-extraction), final check via Google Scholar API; 'hallucinated citations' are defined as the estimated EXCESS of unmatched citations above the pre-LLM (pre-late-2022) baseline, estimated by regression - not a direct count of individually classified references. Headline counts as printed: 'a conservative estimate of 146,932 hallucinated citations in 2025 alone' across the four corpora; estimated hallucination rates as of August 2025: 0.39% (arXiv), 0.21% (bioRxiv), 1.91% (SSRN), 0.27% (PMC); monthly estimates Aug 2025: 3,353 (arXiv), 478 (bioRxiv), 767 (SSRN), 8,140 (PMC); proportion of papers containing at least one hallucinated reference rose by 2 to 23 percentage points across datasets (no single pooled paper-level count printed). Audit definition of fabricated/non-existent reference as printed: a cited reference whose title cannot be matched to any record in the ground-truth databases after all cleaning and lookup steps. Funding: no funding statement found in the preprint text (not reported).
